title: Alignment hub: one-pager & signal map for upcoming all-hands
content:
Purpose: quick-reference one-pager and signal map to align exec asks, OKR drafts, and the Q2 all-hands run-of-show. This is a living working doc for ops + execs to iterate speaker order, asks, and one-line metrics to surface.

Summary / elevator:
- Primary ask to org: prioritize reliability and predictable unit economics for customers running inference at scale. Tie messaging to three customer stories (hosted API scale-up, Dedicated SLA win, private deployment pilot with finance/regulatory constraints).
- Objective of the all-hands: make the operating priorities tangible (what teams will be measured on), remove ambiguity about exec asks, and give managers a small list of concrete actions for next 6 weeks.

Topline narrative (3 bullets):
1) We built the scaffolding — now prioritize reliability and cost optimization across customer workloads. Show one concrete outcome (e.g., 17% cost reduction on small-batch web workloads after caching rollout).
2) Invest in rollout and observability: rollouts + regressions detection + automation = fewer hot fixes and better SLO attainment.
3) Scale readiness: Dedicated and Private pipelines need predictable capacity plans and on-call readiness. We'll announce targeted hiring and ops investments.

OKR drafts (candidate wording) — link to OKR board: JIRA RDW-1987
- Objective A: Reduce hosted API mean latency at p50/p95 when under 90th percentile load by 20% (owner: Eng Serving Runtime)
  - KR A1: Roll out prefix caching to 3 high-volume customers (owner: caching team) — target: 3/3 by end of Q2
  - KR A2: Reduce p95 request queuing time by 50% for model-family X (owner: infra)
  - KR A3: End-to-end synthetic test coverage for model fallbacks (owner: release-eng)
- Objective B: Improve unit economics for enterprise inference
  - KR B1: Deploy quantized model variants for 4 top customer workloads and measure cost delta (owner: optimize)
  - KR B2: Publish public cost/perf heuristics + console recommendations (owner: product-hosted-api)
- Objective C: Customer trust & compliance
  - KR C1: Ship Private deployment checklist and KMS integration playbook (owner: security)
  - KR C2: SLA-incidents runbook + one-table customer-facing escalation timeline (owner: customer-success)

Exec update bullets (what execs should say, 90s each):
- CEO (30–60s): vision recap (serving > model ownership), what success looks like this year (customers achieving production stability and unit-cost wins)
- CTO (90s): state of runtime — metrics (p50/p95, throughput), big wins (new kernel set, batching improvements), and near-term blockers
- Head of Product (60s): roadmap highlights (rollouts, console features, optimize toolkit), and where we need engineering help
- Head of Sales/CS (60s): top three enterprise wins and one ask from engineering (e.g., predictable capacity for Dedicated customers)

Signal map: what to surface for each audience (managers / engineers / sales / customers)
- Managers: OKRs, measurable ownerable KRs, resource asks. Action: publish manager playbook with two-step weekly check-ins.
- Engineers: concrete rollout timelines, incident playbooks, sandboxes for testing quantized models. Action: open office hours schedule + test harness link.
- Sales/CS: customer success stories, capacity commitments, SLA language. Action: one-pager for AE and CSMs explaining fallback behavior.
- Customers (public comms after all-hands): short note with links to our perf benchmarks and roadmap highlights.

Run-of-show (high level):
- 00:00–00:05 — CEO open + framing
- 00:05–00:07 — Culture highlight + shoutouts
- 00:07–00:17 — CTO deep-dive (runtime metrics + demo snippet)
- 00:17–00:30 — Product + Optimize (feature announcements + console demo)
- 00:30–00:35 — Customer success story (video clip + 2-min panel)
- 00:35–00:45 — Breakout/manager micro-sessions (optional)
- 00:45–00:50 — Ask + closures (What we need from teams)
- 00:50–01:00 — Open Q&A (managed via moderator)

Speaker prep notes / callouts:
- Tech demo must show before/after latency for a small HBW customer; avoid internal debugging screens. Pre-record a 90s clip.
- Product demo: focus on console recommendation card and cost delta visualization.
- CS/customer story: give the customer 3 talking points they can reuse publicly.

Asks (owner, deadline):
- Prepare manager playbook and send to managers — owner: Lina Vargas — due: 2026-02-28
- Finalize OKR wording and commit owners — owner: Priya Kapoor + Ethan Morris — due: 2026-02-25
- Pre-record demo clip (runtime) — owner: Samir Patel — due: 2026-02-20
- Publish customer-facing summary post all-hands — owner: Rowan Li — due: 2026-03-09

Risks / open questions (callouts for execs)
- Risk: demo instability — mitigation: pre-record + fallback slide (Samir)
- Risk: messaging ambiguity between Hosted vs Dedicated capabilities — mitigation: explicit one-liner for each product, to be approved by Head of Product
- Open question: do we announce Dedicated capacity expansions publicly or limit to enterprise-only comms? (Sales -> decision by 2026-02-22)

Proposed short manager checklist (to cascade):
- 1-line summary of all-hands + 3 team-level actions
- Confirm owner for each KR in team OKRs
- Join the ops sync next week to review runway

Appendix (quick links & artifacts):
- OKR board (JIRA): RDW-1987
- Run-of-show draft (this doc thread): slack #allhands-prep
- Demo PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quarterly-slate/pull/42
- Manager playbook (draft): confluence.company/manager-playbook-allhands

Notes to self / rough fragments (do not finalize yet):
- Consider short customer panel instead of one 5-min interview (makes the segment more dynamic)
- Ask: keep asks under 3 per team. Managers push back early if overloaded.
- Action: capture top 5 post-all-hands issues into a triage board and assign owners within 48h.

Quick timeline (milestones):
- 2026-02-20: demos recorded + deck content locked
- 2026-02-25: OKRs finalized and managers notified
- 2026-03-02: rehearsal with speakers
- 2026-03-09: all-hands (date tentative; confirm room/video infra)

Raw/working notes (snippets):
- "If we can show 10–15% cost improvement in our public case studies, that dramatically changes the sales convo."
- "We need a one-slide fallback explanation for each product: hosted -> automatic fallbacks; dedicated -> reserved capacity; private -> customer managed upgrades."
- Jira quick refs: RDW-2040 (caching rollout), RDW-2101 (quantization experiments), RDW-1999 (private deployment checklist)

Next steps (this doc):
- Collab owners: please add comments inline. We'll freeze the deck 5 business days before rehearsal.

-- Priya (draft owner)
